title: Oregon's 1st Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The general election for Oregon's 1st Congressional District pits incumbent Democrat Suzanne Bonamici, who has held the seat since 2012, against Republican veterinarian Barbara Kahl. The district encompasses northwestern Oregon including the Portland suburbs of Beaverton and Hillsboro, parts of Portland west of the Willamette River, and Tillamook County. Bonamici won the Democratic primary with 86.6% of the vote, while Kahl secured the Republican nomination with 71.5%. The district has a Cook Partisan Voting Index of D+20 and is rated Solid D by Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball, making Bonamici a strong favorite for re-election.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of mid-2026, likely due to the district's solid Democratic lean and the incumbent's consistent re-election margins above 68%.

candidates.name: Suzanne Bonamici
candidates.summary: Suzanne Bonamici has represented Oregon's 1st Congressional District in the U.S. House since February 2012, when she won a special election to succeed David Wu. Before Congress, she served in the Oregon House of Representatives and was appointed to the Oregon State Senate. Bonamici holds a J.D. from the University of Oregon School of Law and previously worked as an attorney for the Federal Trade Commission and in private practice.

candidates.name: Barbara Kahl
candidates.summary: Barbara Kahl is a veterinarian and the Republican nominee for Oregon's 1st Congressional District. She previously worked at Intel in high-tech finance and purchasing, and has also served as a military ombudsman. Kahl holds a Doctorate in Veterinary Medicine from Oregon State University and emphasizes her family's century-long roots in Northwest Oregon in her campaign.

forecast.rationale: Oregon's 1st CD is rated D+20 by Cook PVI and unanimously rated Solid D by Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball. Incumbent Democrat Suzanne Bonamici has held the seat since 2012, consistently winning general elections with over 68% of the vote. She won the 2026 Democratic primary with 86.6%, while Republican nominee Barbara Kahl, a first-time candidate, won her primary with 71.5%. No public polling has been conducted, reflecting the district's lack of competitiveness. The strong Democratic fundamentals, long incumbency, and absence of any contrary indicators support a Safe Democratic forecast, though the absence of polling prevents high confidence.
